extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, member societies, mathematical institutes, potential contributors and advertisers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive criteria for content suitable for the EMS Magazine (types of articles, audience, publication format, and licensing). Aimed at prospective authors and advertisers considering contributions or placements in the quarterly EMS Magazine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope / Acceptable content types
rubrics_metrics.description: The EMS Magazine is the journal of record of the European Mathematical Society, featuring survey articles on current research topics, contributions outlining trends in scientific development, reports on member societies and institutes, book reviews, a mathematical problems section, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this list as the primary scope criteria for submissions: survey articles, trend/outlook pieces, institutional reports, book reviews, and material for the mathematical problems section. 'And more' indicates flexibility for other mathematically-relevant contributions, but submissions should align with the Magazine's emphasis on surveys, trends, reports, reviews, and problem exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication frequency and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The Magazine is published quarterly in print (March, June, September, December) and is sent to member societies, mathematical institutes and interested individual members of the EMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should expect a quarterly publication cycle and distribution focused on EMS member societies, institutes, and interested individual members; timing and topical relevance to issue schedules may matter for acceptance and planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Access license
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles in the EMS Magazine are published Open Access with a CC BY 4.0 license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions accepted for publication will be released under CC BY 4.0; authors and contributors should be aware this permits reuse and redistribution with attribution. Consider copyright and third-party material permissions accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing / discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles ... are indexed in zbMATH Open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors gain discoverability through indexing in zbMATH Open; authors may highlight this when considering venue fit and visibility for survey or review-style articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising audience and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: It offers an established platform for companies and institutions to advertise products and services to the broad community of mathematicians, statisticians, computer scientists, engineers, and other mathematically-minded professionals who are regular readers of this popular publication. Information on advertisement rates and formats
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertisers should target the broad mathematically-oriented professional readership; the page signals that specific rates and format specifications exist (seek the advertisement rates/formats link for technical requirements and deadlines).
